new_statements.quote: El acento en matlatzinca no es contrastivo a nivel léxico o gramatical, ya que se asigna obligatoriamente a la primera sílaba de la raíz de la palabra,[3] como se muestra a continuación: (20a) síni [ˈsí.ni] 'perro' (b) nú [ˈnú] 'cabeza' (c) nèsíni [nèˈsíni] nè-síni D.PL-PERRO 'los perros' ... (21b) kùtǝwi [kùˈtǝwi] kù-ø-tǝwi 3SG-PRS-CANTAR 'él canta'. Como se puede observar en los ejemplos anteriores, el acento siempre se encuentra en la primera sílaba de la raíz independientemente del carácter polimorfémico de la palabra. Lo anterior se mantiene tanto en el caso de raíces sustantivas en (20) como verbales en (21). [fn. 3: Por consiguiente, en el presente trabajo no se marca el acento en las representaciones fonológicas.]
new_statements.translation: Accent in Matlatzinca is not contrastive at the lexical or grammatical level, since it is obligatorily assigned to the first syllable of the root of the word, as shown below: síni [ˈsíni] 'dog', nú [ˈnú] 'head', nè-síni [nèˈsíni] 'the dogs' ... kù-tǝwi [kùˈtǝwi] 'he sings'. As can be seen in the preceding examples, the accent is always on the first syllable of the root regardless of the polymorphemic character of the word. This holds for noun roots (20) as well as verb roots (21). [fn. 3: Consequently, accent is not marked in the phonological representations in this work.]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is predictable and non-contrastive: it falls on the first syllable of the lexical root; prefixes/proclitic inflectional formatives (nè-, thè-, kù-, té-) are unstressed, so stress is word-initial only in unprefixed words. The language is otherwise tonal (two level tones, H and L, with roots bearing tone on their first syllable; §2.1.4).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in Carranza 2013. (Cazes 1971: 199-200, under an older accent-based analysis, allowed 2-3 non-adjacent accents in words of five or more syllables, with affixes carrying their own fixed accent.)
new_statements.exceptions: None in Carranza 2013 (roots are mono- or disyllabic; a few lexicalized compounds like šúyòwi 'coyote' noted under tone, fn. 5). Palancar & Carranza 2021 fn. 6 add that monosyllabic inflectional formatives are often unstressed and clitic-like. Cazes 1971 gives a conflicting older description in which disyllables may be accented on either syllable (kaki 'yo' vs imó 'pie') and tone is derived from accent; modern work (Carranza 2013, 2015; Palancar & Carranza) instead treats tone as lexical and stress as root-initial.
new_statements.domain_note: Morphological/phonological word in isolation (citation forms with IPA stress marks); stress stated relative to the root, not the word edge. Interaction with the H/L tone system not analysed beyond 'roots receive tone on the first syllable'.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources examined describe the Matlatzinca of San Francisco Oxtotilpan (municipio de Temascaltepec, Estado de México), the only surviving Matlatzinca variety = Glottolog sanf1262 / ISO mat. Cazes 1971 calls it 'maclasinca de Nsampaanchu' (Nsampaanchu = the town's native name). Pascacio Montijo 2017 concerns 16th-century colonial Matlatzinca (Castro's Vocabulario), not the modern language. Not to be confused with Atzingo Matlatzinca / Ocuilteco (atzi1235, ISO ocu).

sources.note: §2.1.3 'El acento' (pp. 14-15): accent is not contrastive lexically or grammatically; it is obligatorily assigned to the first syllable of the root regardless of how many affixes the word carries (síni [ˈsíni], nè-síni [nèˈsíni], kù-tǝwi [kùˈtǝwi]); therefore accent is left unmarked. §2.1.4: Matlatzinca is tonal with two tones (H, L), roots bear tone on their first syllable.

sources.citation: Cazes, Daniel. 1971. La lengua maclasinca de Nsampaanchu, San Francisco Oxtotilpan. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 60: 191-232. doi:10.3406/jsa.1971.2074
sources.note: pp. 199-200 (§§e-g 'Obligatoriedad del acento', 'Tonismo ocasionado por el acento', 'Patrones de acentuación'): older analysis with accent primary and syllable tone derived from position relative to the accent; geminate vowels and monosyllables always accented; affixes have an invariable accent or none, and a root accent shifts rightward to avoid clash; words of up to 5 syllables carry 1-2 accents, longer ones 2-3, never adjacent; disyllables may be accented on 1st or 2nd syllable (mbaani 'casa', kaki 'yo', imó 'pie'); trisyllables on 1st, 2nd, or 1st+3rd.
